subject.title: fix(codex): keep omitted-final source replies from releasing the turn

question: Which Codex source-reply terminal contract should become canonical for the linked regression: this PR's omitted-as-progress behavior with the completed marker preserved, the competing branch's broader classifier change, or a maintainer replacement?
rationale: Both open PRs target the same high-risk message lifecycle, but differ on recovery telemetry and tool-owned termination; tests alone cannot establish the intended exactly-once channel contract.

options.title: Use this branch after live proof
options.body: Keep the narrower explicit-final release rule and preserved completion marker, then require a live channel continuation and recovery transcript before merge.

options.title: Adopt the competing branch
options.body: Select https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107274 only after it preserves or atomically redesigns exactly-once recovery and supplies equivalent live proof.

options.title: Create a maintainer replacement
options.body: Close both contributor branches only after a narrow owner-authored replacement exists and proves the same progress, final, and recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Use this branch after live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the narrower explicit-final release rule and preserved completion marker, then require a live channel continuation and recovery transcript before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and merged the current Codex message-tool-only completion behavior, making them the strongest available owner for its terminal and recovery semantics.
